nextStoryContext: Fixed the reviewer-filed WARNING (test/release-workflow.test.ts:64): the attest-step guard's four-binary assertions were tautological -- they asserted expect(workflow).toContain('dist/gateship-<target>') against the WHOLE workflow text, so they stayed green even if the attest step's own subject-path were mutated to a glob (dist/gateship-*) that never literally contains any of the four asserted substrings, because the later `gh release create` block already lists all four literal paths regardless. Fix mirrors the file's own existing releaseCreateBlock slicing technique (lines 36-41): added an attestStepBlock sliced from `uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v4` to the next `\n      - name:` step boundary, and rebound the four toContain assertions plus a new `attestStepIdx > -1` presence assertion onto that block instead of the whole-file `workflow` string. Verified the fix is falsifiable by mutation BEFORE committing: temporarily rewrote the committed .github/workflows/release.yml's attest step subject-path list to the single-line glob `dist/gateship-*` (Python script, backed up first), re-ran `bun test test/release-workflow.test.ts` and confirmed exactly 1 of 5 tests failed (the four-binary test, with the expected 'Expected to contain: dist/gateship-darwin-arm64' / 'Received: ...subject-path: dist/gateship-*' diagnostic), then restored the original file byte-for-byte from the backup and re-ran the suite to confirm all 5 pass again before touching anything else. The SHA256SUMS.txt assertion, the permissions-block assertion, and the release-create-block assertions were already correctly scoped per the story description and were left untouched. Full spine clean: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 6007 pass / 0 fail across 359 files, bun run check:all all sub-gates ok (test, embed-vendor, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, skip-ratchet). No file-size/coverage budget raises needed (net +21/-5 lines in one existing file, well under ceiling). scripts/cam/prd.json's US-R1-001/US-R1-002/US-005 priority renumber and the US-R2-001/US-R2-002 entries were pre-existing uncommitted working-tree state before this story (left untouched per AGENT.md -- supervisor is the sole prd.json writer). This closes out the CAM-495 review round 2 findings (US-R2-001 done in the prior story, US-R2-002 done here); no further round-2 findings are known pending in prd.json as of this handoff.
